{{Quote|Apology accepted, Captain Needa.|Darth Vader, after killing Needa|audio=SarcasmAcceptedLordVader-ESB.flac|<ref name="TESB" />}}
'''Lorth Needa''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] officer in the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] and the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. He served as [[Lieutenant Commander/Legends|lieutenant commander]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] [[Carrack-class light cruiser/Legends|''Carrack''-class cruiser]] [[Integrity (Carrack-class)/Legends|''Integrity'']] in [[Home Fleet Strike Group Five/Legends|Home Fleet Strike Group Five]] of the [[Coruscant Defense Fleet/Legends|Coruscant Home Fleet]] during the [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|Battle of Coruscant]], in which he was prepared to destroy the [[Invisible Hand/Legends|''Invisible Hand'']], [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]] of [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] [[Supreme Commander of the Droid Armies/Legends|Supreme Commander]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]], should the [[Kaleesh/Legends|Kaleesh]] [[General/Legends|general]] be unable to prove that [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] was being held captive aboard the [[Providence-class carrier/destroyer/Legends|warship]]. During the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] era, Needa was promoted to [[Captain/Legends|captain]] of the [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer]] [[Avenger/Legends|''Avenger'']] by [[Fleet Admiral/Legends|Fleet Admiral]] [[Kendal Ozzel/Legends|Kendal Ozzel]] and assigned to [[Supreme Commander (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Supreme Commander]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader's]] [[Death Squadron/Legends|Death Squadron]], often being tasked with following up on certain leads regarding the location of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance's]] hidden headquarters. Captain Needa served as one of [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] Ozzel's [[Advisor/Legends|advisors]], earning him the distrust of both [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] Vader and [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] Palpatine.

In the aftermath of the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], where General [[Maximilian Veers/Legends|Maximilian Veers's]] assault on [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] forced the Rebels into fleeing, Needa and the ''Avenger'' were charged with capturing [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo's]] [[YT-1300 light freighter/Legends|YT-1300 light freighter]], the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']], and her crew. The ''Falcon'' outran the pursuing [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]] and hid within the [[Hoth asteroid field/Legends|Hoth asteroid field]], but the ''Avenger'' plunged into the [[Asteroid field/Legends|field]], intent on completing its assignment. The search proved to be hazardous as the warship sustained damage, and its [[Gunner/Legends|gunners]] were forced to fire on the [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroids]] rather than remain alert for the elusive [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]]. Nevertheless, when the ''Falcon'' emerged from the maelstrom, the ''Avenger'' was right behind the freighter. Before Needa could detain the craft, Solo charged the ''Avenger'' and landed on a blind spot on the aft of the destroyer's conning tower; as a result, the destroyer's sensors could not find the vessel. Believing to have failed his mission, Needa went to the [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|Star Dreadnought]] [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']] to personally apologize to Vader. The [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] accepted his apology after [[Telekinesis/Legends#Choking powers|making sure]] that the captain would never fail again. Two [[Imperial Navy Trooper/Legends|Imperial Navy troopers]] then dragged Needa's lifeless body away.

==Biography==
===Republic Navy service===
{{Quote|Ten minutes from now, I will have either your surrender, or confirmation that Supreme Chancellor Palpatine is alive, unharmed&mdash;and present&mdash;or ''Invisible Hand'' will be destroyed.''"<br />"''Wait&mdash;you can't simply&mdash;''"<br />"''Ten minutes, General. Needa out.|Lieutenant Commander Needa and General Grievous during the Battle of Coruscant|<ref name="ROTS novel" />}}
A [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] from [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]],<ref name="CE" /> Lorth Needa was a veteran command officer, having served in [[Home Fleet Strike Group Five/Legends|Strike Group Five]] of the [[Coruscant Defense Fleet/Legends|Coruscant Home Fleet]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. In the [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|Battle of Coruscant]], in which the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] launched a surprise attack on the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], [[Lieutenant Commander/Legends|Lieutenant Commander]] Needa served as commanding officer of the [[Carrack-class light cruiser/Legends|''Carrack''-class cruiser]] [[Integrity (Carrack-class)/Legends|''Integrity'']], which was part of the Republic defenses. Together with two other [[Carrack-class light cruiser/Legends|''Carrack''-class cruisers]] and a [[Dreadnaught-class heavy cruiser/Legends|''Dreadnaught''-class heavy cruiser]], Needa trapped the [[Providence-class carrier/destroyer/Legends|''Providence''-class carrier/destroyer]] [[Invisible Hand/Legends|''Invisible Hand'']] as it was trying to escape, and demanded the surrender of its [[Commander/Legends|commander]], the Separatist [[Supreme Commander of the Droid Armies/Legends|Supreme Commander]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]]. During this encounter, Needa did not believe the [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] [[General/Legends|general's]] claims that [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], leader of the Republic, was aboard the ''Invisible Hand''. The Republic commander told the [[Kaleesh/Legends|Kaleesh]] [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] via [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]] that he had ten [[Standard minute/Legends|minutes]] to prove his claim&mdash;if he could not, the ships of Strike Group Five would open fire on the Separatist [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]] and destroy it. General Grievous did not surrender, but Chancellor Palpatine was rescued by [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi Generals]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]].<ref name="ROTS novel" />

The ''Invisible Hand'' was severely damaged by Republic fire, and while Grievous fled, the two [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] began to [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] the remains of the ''Hand'' to crash-land on Coruscant. Needa watched, greatly impressed, as Skywalker skillfully maneuvered the ship into the capital [[Planet/Legends|world's]] [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]]. The lieutenant commander informed the [[Grand Master/Legends|Jedi Grand Master]], [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]], via hologram of Kenobi and Skywalker's success; he also told the diminutive Jedi to have the surface-defense systems stand down and a flight of [[Emergency firespeeder/Legends|emergency firespeeders]] deployed to attempt to douse the fires on the ''Hand''{{'s}} hull. Yoda thanked him for his valiant assistance during the battle, and as the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master's]] hologram faded away, Needa watched helplessly as the ''Hand'' continued to fall, doubting that Skywalker would be able to succeed. Though the battle had been won, he feared that should the Chancellor perish, the war would be lost. Nevertheless, Skywalker succeeded in his endeavor, and Palpatine survived unharmed.<ref name="ROTS novel" />

Shortly thereafter, Palpatine declared himself [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] and reformed the Republic into the first [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], declaring the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] an enemy of the state. As part of the subsequent [[Imperialization/Legends|Imperialization]], the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]] was reorganized into the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]].<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref> Two weeks into Palpatine's [[New Order/Legends|New Order]], the Emperor and the [[Supreme Commander (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Supreme Commander]],<ref name="kenner">{{KennerCite|set=Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (toy line)|pack=Darth Vader vs. Prince Xizor|link=soteKxizor-vader.asp}}</ref> [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Vader&mdash;formerly known as the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] Anakin Skywalker&mdash;spoke before a gathering of naval officers and announced that they were all required to serve the navy in the unstable times that would follow the Clone Wars, and that any who dissented would be [[Emperor's purge|purged]] from the military.<ref name="Republic 78">[[Republic 78|''Republic'' 78]]</ref>

===Captain of the ''Avenger''===
{{Quote|&hellip; the idea that the so-called Rebellion could be responsible for the destruction of an Imperial Star Destroyer is completely ludicrous.|Captain Needa, following the loss of the ''Desolator''|<ref name="Isis note">According to ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', the Rebels abandoned Isis not long after the Battle of Yavin, placing ''[[The Isis Coordinates]]'' around 0.5 ABY.</ref>}}
[[File:YouHaveToBeKidding-ESB.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Lorth Needa on the bridge of the ''Avenger'' during the pursuit of the ''Millennium Falcon'']]
Needa continued to serve in the navy, eventually rising to the rank of [[Captain/Legends|captain]]. [[Fleet Admiral/Legends|Fleet Admiral]] [[Kendal Ozzel/Legends|Kendal Ozzel]], commander of the [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|Star Dreadnought]] [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']] and the Imperial [[Death Squadron/Legends|Death Squadron]], placed Captain Needa in command of the [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer]] [[Avenger/Legends|''Avenger'']],<ref name="GG3">''[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back]]''</ref> a position previously held by Captain [[Ferdas]].<ref name="Death of a Rebel Base">{{WEGCite|story=Death of a Rebel Base|book=Imperial Sourcebook|reprint=1}}</ref> The ''Avenger'', having gone through many captains within its history, was noted to be an unlucky [[Starship/Legends|ship]] when it came to its commanders.<ref name="FF4">[[The Official Star Wars Fact File 4|''The Official Star Wars Fact File'' 4]]</ref> As a member of Death Squadron&mdash;Vader's personal [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]]&mdash;Needa aided in the mission to discover and destroy the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebels']] hidden headquarters.<ref name="GG3" /> While serving in the [[Squadron/Legends|unit]], Captain Needa gained a reputation for efficiency in quelling uprisings in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]], and [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] Ozzel assigned ''Avenger'' to the "point" position in Death Squadron. Needa became one of Ozzel's closest [[Advisor/Legends|advisors]].<ref name="Needa card">{{CCG|set=Dagobah Limited|cardname=Captain Needa}}</ref>

The [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] between the Empire and the Rebel Alliance had increased in magnitude since the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|destruction]] of the Empire's planet-destroying [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star I]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]] at [[Yavin Prime/Legends|Yavin Prime]],<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> and the Empire had become determined to find and destroy the Rebels' new base of operations.<ref name="TESB" /> To speed up this search, Admiral Ozzel often sent Needa and the ''Avenger'' off on missions independent from the rest of the Death Squadron to check on certain leads relating to the Rebels' hidden command base.<ref name="GG3" /> Regardless of Ozzel's trust in the ''Avenger''{{'s}} captain, [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] Vader and [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] Palpatine felt quite different. The two [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]] distrusted the admiral and all of his advisors,<ref name="Needa card" /> resulting in the execution of any of them for the simplest of mistakes.<ref name="GG3" />

Around [[0 ABY/Legends|0.5 ABY]],<ref name="Isis note" /> a group of Rebels trapped aboard the Star Destroyer [[Desolator (Imperial-class)/Legends|''Desolator'']], heading for the Rebel base on the planet [[Isis/Legends|Isis]], managed to replace Isis's coordinates in the warship's [[Navigation computer/Legends|navicomputer]] with those of the rogue [[Star/Legends|star]] [[G-138]]. As a result of the sabotage, the ''Desolator'' collided with G-138 and was destroyed. The [[Imperial News Bureau]] claimed the ship's destruction was the result of a [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] malfunction, denying that there was any Rebel involvement. Needa was quoted in the Bureau's announcement, saying such thoughts of Rebel sabotage were "ludicrous."<ref name="Isis">''[[The Isis Coordinates]]'', the events of which were confirmed by ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''{{'s}} entry on the ''Desolator''</ref>

As the hunt for the Rebels' headquarters continued, Needa was one of the captains tasked with sending out thousands of [[Viper probe droid/Legends|Viper probe droids]] to the [[Hoth system/Legends|Hoth]], [[Tokmia system/Legends|Tokmia]], [[Allyuen system/Legends|Allyuen]], and countless other star systems to expand the search,<ref name="Freedom's Winter">{{ESBRadio|Freedom's Winter}}</ref> in conjunction with the [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] ''[[Stalker/Legends|Stalker]]''.<ref name="Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref><ref name="Stalker CCG">{{CCG|set=Hoth Limited|cardname=''Stalker''}}</ref><ref name="SWE">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref><ref name="BTM">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref> Ultimately, one of the [[Probe droid/Legends|probe droids]] of this operation discovered the existence of a [[Planetary shield/Legends|planetary shield]] generator on the [[Water/Legends|ice]] world of [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]].<ref name="Atlas" /> Though Ozzel was skeptical of the find, Vader insisted that the generator marked the location of the Alliance's command base. The Lord of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] ordered Death Squadron into [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] with the sixth world of the Hoth system as their target.<ref name="TESB" />

===Battle of Hoth and the hunt for the ''Millennium Falcon''===
[[File:WhatTheKriff-ESB.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Needa and his bridge crew duck as the ''Millennium Falcon'' narrowly misses the ''Avenger''{{'s}} bridge.]]
{{Quote|Get a shuttle ready. I shall assume full responsibility for losing them, and apologize to Lord Vader.|Needa, after failing to capture the ''Millennium Falcon''|audio=ThisIsABadIdea-ESB.flac|<ref name="TESB" />}}
Before the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]] could even commence, Ozzel died at Vader's hand for his blunder in bringing Death Squadron out of hyperspace too close to Hoth, a move that alerted the Rebels to the Imperials' presence and allowed them to raise their [[Deflector shield/Legends|shield]] and begin the evacuation of [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]]. While the battle raged on between the Rebels and General [[Maximilian Veers/Legends|Maximilian Veers's]] [[Blizzard Force/Legends|Blizzard Force]] of [[All Terrain Armored Transport/Legends|AT-ATs]] and [[All Terrain Scout Transport/Legends|AT-STs]] on the planet below, the fleet of Star Destroyers was charged with preventing the fleeing [[GR-75 medium transport/Legends|GR-75 medium transports]] and other Rebel craft from escaping.<ref name="TESB" /> Seventeen of the thirty GR-75 transports were destroyed by the Imperial fleet,<ref name="Of Possible Futures">{{StoryCite|story=Of Possible Futures: The Tale of Zuckuss and 4-LOM|book=Tales of the Bounty Hunters}}</ref> but destroyers such as Captain [[Xamuel Lennox]]'s [[Rebel Dream|''Tyrant'']] were disabled by the Rebels' [[V-150 Planet Defender/Legends|planetary ion cannon]]. As the Imperials claimed victory, the [[YT-1300 light freighter/Legends|YT-1300 light freighter]] [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']], piloted by the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and his [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] co-pilot [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]], escaped from Echo Base's main hangar with [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] aboard. Captain Needa and the ''Avenger'' were charged with the pursuit and capture of the ''Falcon'' and its crew.<ref name="TESB" />

The ''Avenger'' did just that, and the ''Falcon'', with an inoperable [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]], was unable to flee the [[Star system/Legends|system]]. However, Solo's light [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] outmaneuvered the Star Destroyer and nearly caused it to collide with another pursuing destroyer. After chasing the ''Falcon'' into the [[Hoth asteroid field/Legends|Hoth asteroid field]], the ''Avenger'' lost track of the freighter when it sought shelter in a cave on one of the larger [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroids]].<ref name="TESB" /> Nevertheless, the destroyer ventured into the [[Asteroid field/Legends|asteroid field]] at Vader's command. The ''Avenger'' suffered damage while it searched for the elusive ''Falcon'', and the [[Gunner/Legends|gunners]] stationed onboard were forced to focus their attention on incoming asteroids rather than looking out for the YT-1300 freighter.<ref name="GG3" /> While present during a holographic conference of twenty [[Battleship/Legends|battleship]] commanders aboard the ''Executor'', the Needa informed Vader that it had been some time since the ''Millennium Falcon'' had appeared on the ''Avenger''{{'s}} [[Sensor/Legends|sensors]].<ref name="ESB novel">[[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back'' novel]]</ref> Needa, his hologram faded and disrupted by static,<ref name="BTM" /> noted to Vader that, given the amount of damage that the Imperial fleet had sustained due to asteroid collisions, the ''Falcon'' had to have been destroyed. However, the Supreme Commander believed otherwise, and he was set on capturing the freighter regardless of the fleet's losses.<ref name="ESB novel" />

===Failure and death===
{{Quote|They are minor criminals! Marginal outlaws! You are inept!''"<br />"''N-no&mdash;Lord Vader&mdash;please&hellip;''"<br />"''And ineptitude is of no use to me or the Empire.''"<br />"''N-no&mdash;my lord&mdash;I beg you&hellip;|Darth Vader and Lorth Needa, shortly before the latter's death|audio=ImperialManagementTechniques-ESBRadio.flac|<ref name="New Allies">{{ESBRadio|New Allies, New Enemies}}</ref>}}
[[File:WorstSoreThroatEver-ESB.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Needa is telekinetically strangled to death by Darth Vader.]]
The ''Millennium Falcon'' eventually reappeared after discovering that the alleged cave it had hidden in was in fact the mouth of a giant [[Exogorth/Legends|space slug]]. The ''Avenger'' managed to spot the freighter as it attempted its escape, and Needa had a priority signal sent to the ''Executor'' to inform Ozzel's replacement as Admiral, [[Firmus Piett/Legends|Firmus Piett]], that the ''Falcon'' was about to be captured.<ref name="TESB" /> A link was established on the [[Star Dreadnought/Legends|Star Dreadnought's]] [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]], allowing those assembled&mdash;including a group of [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] that Vader had gathered to hunt down the ''Falcon'' and her crew&mdash;to listen to Needa as he gave orders during the pursuit.<ref name="Payback">{{StoryCite|story=Payback: The Tale of Dengar|book=Tales of the Bounty Hunters}}</ref> While the ''Avenger'' pursued the ''Falcon'' out of the asteroid field and into the neighboring [[Anoat system/Legends|Anoat system]], the YT-1300 moved into what Needa had assumed to be attack position.<ref name="TESB" /> Rushing to the [[Viewport/Legends|viewports]], Needa watched with his horrified command crew as the ''Falcon'' charged the bridge, setting off alarms throughout the Imperial warship. Needa asked if their [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shields]] were up before commenting that Solo must have been insane to attempt to ram the destroyer head-on.<ref name="ESB novel" />

Needa and his crew dropped to the floor in terror, but Solo veered his ship up sharply, narrowly missing the Star Destroyer's bridge. As he rose from the deck, Needa ordered his crew to track the ship, wondering if they would attempt another pass.<ref name="ESB novel" /> The ''Avenger''{{'s}} logistics officer, Commander [[Nemet/Legends|Nemet]], reported that the ''Falcon'' had vanished from their sensors&mdash;unknown to the Imperials, Solo had cut his ship's power and landed on a blind spot on the conning tower<ref name="TESB" /> of the ''Avenger''.<ref name="DB" /> Needa dispelled the idea that the ''Falcon'' may have possessed a [[Cloaking device/Legends|cloaking device]], and the deck officer suggested that the freighter had simply gone into hyperspace. The captain, both angry and confused, wondered why they would have attempted such a daring maneuver only to flee the system. Flabbergasted, Needa wondered how the ship could have escaped him.<ref name="ESB novel" /> Seconds later, Needa's communications officer, [[M'Kae/Legends|M'Kae]], reported that Vader demanded an update on the pursuit.<ref name="TESB" />

Needa ordered his ship to rendezvous with the ''Executor'' so he could personally apologize for losing Vader's prey,<ref name="TESB" /> believing that it was the honorable thing to do.<ref name="CSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> However, he had the ''Avenger'' perform one last sensor sweep of the area for their elusive quarry&mdash;to no avail.<ref name="ESB novel" /> Needa ordered a [[TIE/sh VIP shuttle]] to be prepared for his visit to the ''Executor'', departing the ''Avenger'' for the last time. Upon arriving, he immediately went to the [[Star Dreadnought/Legends|Star Dreadnought's]] bridge, where the captain met with the Supreme Commander.<ref name="TESB" /> Needa apologized, but Vader soon lost his patience, calling the man inept for failing to capture a mere group of outlaws. Needa knew that Vader's anger<ref name="New Allies" />&mdash;combined with his own failure<ref name="ESB novel" />&mdash;would lead to a certain [[Death/Legends|death]], so the captain begged for his life. But the Dark Lord noted that the Empire had no use for the captain's ineptness;<ref name="New Allies" /> having finished berating Needa, Vader [[Telekinesis/Legends#Choking powers|telekinetically throttled]] him to death as he had done to Kendal Ozzel earlier. The Supreme Commander then formally accepted the captain's apology, and the dead man's body was dragged from the bridge by two [[Imperial Navy Trooper/Legends|Imperial Navy troopers]].<ref name="TESB" />

===Legacy===
[[File:VaderNeeda-TESB40.png|thumb|right|200px|Darth Vader looms over Needa's body.]]
{{Quote|Hey, it was your cousin who was martyred by Darth Vader after he let Han Solo escape Hoth. After all, your cousin had Rebel sympathies that he only confided in you, which is why he let Solo escape. Your having been punished with this duty proves the Empire suspected him, but could prove nothing.|Pedetsen to Virar Needa|<ref name="Wedge's Gamble">''[[X-Wing: Wedge's Gamble]]''</ref>}}
As a consequence of Lorth Needa's failure, members of the [[Needa family]] were purged from the Imperial military on Darth Vader's orders. His first cousin once removed, [[Virar Needa|Virar]], had been attending the [[Imperial Academy/Legends|Imperial Academy]] during the Battle of Hoth, and as he was not ambitious, he had been allowed to live. Many family members, from Virar's grandparents to cousins, however, were killed. Virar became the commander of one of Coruscant's [[Orbital Solar Energy Transfer Satellite|orbital mirrors]], [[OSETS 2711]]. His subordinates, including [[Cadet/Legends|Cadet]] [[Pedetsen]], had suggested&mdash;without any concrete proof&mdash;that Lorth had failed in capturing the ''Millennium Falcon'' because he had sympathies to the Rebel Alliance. Pedetsen stated that Virar had been placed on OSETS 2711 because the Empire could not prove Lorth's alleged Rebel loyalties. Virar was even willing to believe this.<ref name="Wedge's Gamble" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Thank you, Lieutenant Commander. Valiant service for the Republic you have done today&mdash;and the gratitude of the Jedi Order you have earned.|Jedi Master Yoda, to Lieutenant Commander Needa during the Battle of Coruscant|<ref name="ROTS novel" />}}
[[File:SWE-CaptainNeeda.png|thumb|right|200px|Despite his long career, Lorth Needa was executed for his failure to capture the ''Millennium Falcon'']]
Lorth Needa was an efficient commander and could be ruthless at times,<ref name="GG3" /> a trait he exhibited during the Battle of Coruscant, when he threatened to destroy the ''Invisible Hand'' should Grievous choose not to surrender. Later, as Skywalker maneuvered the crumbling ''Hand'' into Coruscant's atmosphere for a landing, Needa watched in both awe and terror, impressed with Skywalker's great skill but also fearing for the Chancellor's life. A disciplined officer, Needa stood expressionless as the events unfolded, but he still ached in fear, clenching his hands tightly. Though not religious, he asked [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] that should the remnants of the ''Hand'' explode, all aboard would be granted, at the very least, a quick death.<ref name="ROTS novel" />

Needa was an able leader, but both Vader and Palpatine harbored suspicions about him.<ref name="Needa card" /> The captain showed a degree of concern for both his crew and the Death Squadron when he suggested to the Supreme Commander that they pull out of the asteroid field during the search for the ''Millennium Falcon'',<ref name="TESB" /> but Needa's failure in capturing Solo's freighter cemented, in Vader's mind, that the ''Avenger''{{'s}} captain was inept.<ref name="New Allies" /> He had been overconfident in his pursuit of the ''Millennium Falcon'' from Hoth, and this factored into his execution by the Dark Lord of the Sith.<ref name="GG3" /> The captain had decided that personally apologizing to the Supreme Commander was an honorable thing for a man in his position to do, thus also sparing his ship's crew the infamous wrath of his superior;<ref name="CSWE" /> nevertheless, Needa begged for his life as Vader prepared to kill him.<ref name="New Allies" />

In addition to his native [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]],<ref name="TESB" /> Needa was able to speak [[Twi'leki/Legends|Ryl]], the native [[Language/Legends|language]] of the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'leks]] of [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]]. When it came to the policies of the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]], Needa had taken specialized courses to further understand the many facets of Palpatine's doctrine. The captain also possessed a considerable knowledge of the workings of the Imperial Navy that he was in service to.<ref name="RESB">''[[Rebellion Era Sourcebook]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
===Portrayal and name===
Lorth Needa first appeared in the [[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|novelization]] of [[1980]]'s [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''The Empire Strikes Back'']]. Known only as "Captain Needa" in the film, he was portrayed by actor [[Michael Culver]]. In the [[The Empire Strikes Back (radio)|radio adaptation]] of the film, Needa was voiced by [[Nicholas Kepros]]. Needa was not given a first name until [[1996]]'s ''[[X-Wing: Wedge's Gamble]]'', when his first cousin once removed, Virar, revealed his first name to be "Lorth."

In ''The Empire Strikes Back'', a blooper occurred after Vader executed Needa. When the Navy troopers begin to drag away his body, Culver visibly locked his legs in such a way as to help those portraying the Navy troopers to stand him up easier.

===Continuity issues===
{{Quote|The ''Millennium Falcon'' definitely went into light-speed. It is probably on the other side of the galaxy by now. I tried my best.|Needa to Darth Vader, moments before his death, as presented in ''[[The Empire Strikes Back Storybook]]''|<ref name="The Empire Strikes Back Storybook">''[[The Empire Strikes Back Storybook]]''</ref>}}
Different [[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] sources have inconsistently stated whether or not Needa's star destroyer ''Avenger'' was the one that launched the probe droid that landed on Hoth. "[[Freedom's Winter]]" ([[1983]]), the first episode of [[The Empire Strikes Back (radio)|''The Empire Strikes Back'' radio drama]], depicted Captain Needa overseeing the launch of the droid.<ref name="Freedom's Winter" /><ref name="The Empire Strikes Back: The National Public Radio Dramatization">[[The Empire Strikes Back: The National Public Radio Dramatization|''The Empire Strikes Back'': The National Public Radio Dramatization]]</ref> ''[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back]]'' ([[1989]]) followed the radio drama, identifying the ''Avenger'' as the Star Destroyer that launched the Hoth probe. A [[Hoth Limited]] card in the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game]] ([[1996]]) later contradicted this, introducing the ''[[Stalker/Legends|Stalker]]'' as the Star Destroyer that carried out the operation. The ''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' and the PC program ''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]'' (both [[1998]]) followed the card game and named the ''Stalker''. Further adding to the confusion, ''[[Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary]]'' (also 1998) identified the ship as the ''Avenger''. Attempting to clarify the discrepancy, ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' ([[2009]]) states that both ships were responsible for deploying probe droids to the Allyuen, Tokmia, and Hoth systems, without stating with certainty which ship is seen in the film.<ref name="Atlas" />

[[File:Ozzel_death.png|thumb|left|250px|Needa's death, as reused for Ozzel's death in ''Star Wars 40: The Empire Strikes Back: Battleground Hoth'']]
In [[Star Wars (1977) 40|''Star Wars'' (1977) 40]], [[Al Williamson]] and [[Carlos Garzón|Carlos Garzon]] used reference photography of Needa's death for Admiral Ozzel's execution.<ref name="Star Wars 40 mistake">{{SWArchive|url=eu/lit/comics/f20080227/index.html?page=7|text=Checklist: Turning Star Wars Japanese &mdash; Manga Scenes Done Better: Episode V: Death of Admiral Ozzel}}</ref>

In the novelization of ''The Empire Strikes Back'', Needa and the ''Avenger'' take the place of Captain [[Xamuel Lennox]] and the [[Rebel Dream|''Tyrant'']] in the scene where the Rebels' [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannon]] fires on a Star Destroyer approaching Hoth. However, while the ship is merely disabled by the ion blasts in the film, the novelization describes the cannon fire hitting the destroyer's conning tower, setting off explosions that propel the out-of-control warship into the void. Regardless, Needa and the ''Avenger'' reappear in later scenes.

''[[The Empire Strikes Back Storybook]]'' offers an alternate interpretation of Needa's execution that comes into conflict with the dialogue featured in the radio adaptation. In this version, the captain merely states that the ''Millennium Falcon'' has escaped despite his best efforts, before being immediately executed by Darth Vader. The radio adaptation, on the other hand, presents a dialogue that occurs between the two men before Vader telekinetically kills Needa. This article assumes that the radio adaptation illustrates the correct version of the scene.

===Possible appearance===
In the non-[[canon]] [[Star Wars Infinities: The Empire Strikes Back 1|''Star Wars Infinities: The Empire Strikes Back'' 1]], when the ''Falcon'' and crew are escaping Hoth during the Imperial assault, Solo charges the bridge of a Star Destroyer, lands on its conning tower immediately afterward, and drifts away along with the garbage that the destroyer releases before jumping to hyperspace&mdash;a course of events practically identical to Solo's maneuver against the ''Avenger'' in the film. Neither the captain nor the destroyer are named in the comic.
